newsitem.title: UK: Yugoslavia wants syndicated loan in debt overhaul.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslavia wants syndicated loan in debt overhaul.

text.p: Yugoslavia, which this week has been holding talks with creditor banks in London, is aiming to restructure its $2.4 billion in debt with a syndicated loan, bankers said on Tuesday.
The first round of negotiations on Monday ended without an agreement and talks resumed on Tuesday. A delegation from Yugoslavia is headed by deputy prime minister Danko Djunic.

According to official documents obtained by Reuters, Yugoslavia is looking to reduce the amount of principal and interest by 80 percent and issue $481 million via a syndicated loan with a 25-year maturity.
It is also proposing a grace period of nine years before repayment of principal begins.
The key objective outlined in the document was for Yugoslavia to normalise relations with international commercial banks and return to international financial markets.
Other objectives were for it to participate on the securities markets, access diversified sources of finance and increase direct private investment during the process of privatisation.

On Monday after the first day's talks, Djunic told Reuters: "We discussed very seriously for more than three hours and we adjourned with the decision to meet tomorrow morning again to continue with their (banks') questions and clarifications."
"I am satisfied with the course of the meeting."

Technical talks on a possible restructuring or rescheduling of Yugoslavia's London Club debt were last held late in 1996, when sources close to the negotiating team said the talks stumbled over Belgrade presenting an overly optimistic report on the country's economic situation.
